verdicts.reason: A moves the headline above the product and enlarges the legal line to almost subhead size. Its CTA sits left of centre and is jammed against the bottom-left corner, and the sale ribbon has shrunk to an afterthought. B keeps a sensible order (product, headline, offer, CTA) with a strong CTA, but the logo is a speck crammed into the top-right corner, the legal text is still too big, and the ribbon is clipped at the bottom edge where it crowds the CTA.

A's CTA is a tiny pill that is easy to miss and is outweighed by the legal copy. The headline is undersized next to the huge phone, and the ribbon runs off the bottom-right edge. B has the same structure but a properly dominant headline and CTA; its flaws are the tiny corner logo, oversized fine print and the ribbon clipped at the canvas bottom.

A has a clear top-to-bottom order with the product as hero and a prominent CTA. It still has a microscopic corner logo, legal text that is too large, and a ribbon cramped and clipped at the bottom edge. B puts the CTA first, above the headline, and shrinks the phone to an illegible sliver at the bottom. The logo is gone and the headline wraps one word per line ('Make / the'), so it is unusable.

A shrinks the phone hero to a small thumbnail and leaves the orphan '21.' on its own line. The logo is pushed to the bottom inside the decorative circle, so the reading order ends with the brand, and the legal copy is oversized. B keeps the product prominent and the CTA strong, but has a speck-sized logo in the top-right corner and the ribbon clipped at the bottom edge.
